title: Build the Enterprise Facilities agent on Google Cloud

layers.title: Foundation Models
layers.objective: Call a foundation model from code the way every other layer will: a chat turn, a tool-calling turn and an embedding.
learn: One request shape for chat; tool calling: the model asks, your code runs the tool
Embeddings turn text into vectors for search
The model catalogue versus the model id your code uses
build: models.list to see the catalogue; models.get resolves the id your app uses.
generateContent: a chat turn.
generateContent with function declarations (tool calling).
embedContent with text-embedding-005: a paraphrase ranks above unrelated text.
Attach your Model Armor template (chapter 11) to a model call and watch it block a prompt attack.
checks: function calling returns a call or text
simplified: Answers come from one small local open model, not Gemini; quality is far lower.
Standard Gemini model ids resolve as compatibility aliases.

code.text:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=PROJECT, location="us-central1")   # point at the simulator via the standard endpoint setting
r = client.models.generate_content(model=MODEL_ID, contents="Reply with OK.")
print(r.text)

layers.outcome: A model client any layer can import: chat, tool calling and embeddings

layers.title: Agent Runtime
layers.objective: Host a supervisor agent that routes work to Facilities, Maintenance and Analytics sub-agents, one isolated session at a time.
learn: Supervisor and sub-agents: plan, route, synthesise
The agent harness: step, token and cost budgets, checkpoints, timeouts, a kill switch
Session isolation: separate state per session
build: Write the supervisor and three sub-agents (entrypoint agent_engine_app.agent).
Create the Agent Engine from source.
Query it: the supervisor runs the Facilities, Maintenance and Analytics sub-agents.
Query with a second session id and prove isolation.
simplified: Agent code runs in the simulator's own sandbox; Agent Engine scaling and quotas are not modelled.
layers.outcome: A supervisor agent and three sub-agents answering in isolated sessions

layers.title: Tools
layers.objective: Build the tools the agents call: read-only lookups first, then write tools that sit behind approval.
learn: A tool is a function with a clear input and output contract
Read-only tools versus approval-gated write tools
Tool code never trusts its caller
build: Seed Firestore with assets and work orders.
generateUploadUrl, PUT the zip, CreateFunction for kb-search, asset-status, the MCP tool server, approval-decision and create-work-order.
Invoke kb-search (RAG from inside the function).
Invoke asset-status (Firestore read from inside the function).
simplified: Functions run in a simulator sandbox; instance scaling, memory limits and cold starts are not modelled.
layers.outcome: Read-only and approval-gated tools your agents can call

layers.title: Knowledge Pipeline
layers.objective: Turn documents into searchable knowledge, and re-index automatically when a new document lands.
learn: Chunking and why chunk size matters
Embeddings and vector search
Event-driven ingestion: storage event, function, index job
build: Upload the SOPs and manuals to the facilities-docs bucket.
Create the RAG corpus facilities-kb.
import_rag_files from gs://facilities-docs/docs/ and list_rag_files.
Add a bucket notification (OBJECT_FINALIZE) to Pub/Sub.
Eventarc: object finalized, then function, then RAG import (event-driven re-index). A re-uploaded document replaces its old version.
simplified: Embeddings come from a small local model; the vector store is a lightweight engine behind the same API.
layers.outcome: Documents flowing into a searchable knowledge base, re-indexed on every upload

layers.title: Knowledge Search (RAG)
layers.objective: Retrieve the right passages for a question, rank them, and keep the source so answers can cite it.
learn: Vector, keyword and hybrid retrieval
Reranking
Why sources must travel with results
build: retrieveContexts for a boiler question; the boiler SOP ranks first.
retrieveContexts for an air-handler question; the HVAC manual ranks first.
Read the source URI of every context (needed for citations).
Create a Vertex AI Search data store over the same SOP and search it.
simplified: Ranking depends on a small local embedding model.
layers.outcome: Ranked retrieval that keeps the source of every passage

layers.title: Response Generation
layers.objective: Answer in plain language from the retrieved documents, with citations, and filter sensitive data out before the user sees it.
learn: Grounding: answer only from retrieved text
Citations and how to check them
Output guardrails: sensitive-data masking and policy filters
build: Generate an answer from retrieved contexts and cite the sources.
sanitizeModelResponse on the agent answer: sensitive data is flagged.
The clean agent answer passes the output filter.
generateContent with the RAG retrieval tool returns an answer with groundingMetadata.
simplified: Model Armor is a deterministic filter set, not Google's trained classifiers.
Answer quality is that of a small local model.
layers.outcome: Grounded answers with citations and sensitive data masked

layers.title: Agent Memory
layers.objective: Give the agent memory: short-term events inside a session and long-term facts it can retrieve later.
learn: Short-term memory is the events of one session
Long-term memory outlives a session
Scope memory per user and tenant; mind retention and poisoning
build: Create the memory host engine facilities_memory.
Create a session for the user and append a user turn and an agent turn.
List the events to replay the session.
Memory Bank: create a fact and retrieve it by similarity (long-term).
Generate memories from a conversation (model fact extraction).
simplified: Fact extraction uses the small local model, so extracted facts are rougher than production.
layers.outcome: Short-term session memory and retrievable long-term facts

layers.title: Agent Gateway
layers.objective: Put one governed door in front of the tools: a tool catalogue, a policy check on every call and a rate limit.
learn: Tool catalogue over MCP
Policy on every tool call: identity, role, attributes
Throttling, schema validation and audit with the user identity
build: Register the facilities MCP server in the agent registry.
Create facilities-gateway and wait for ACTIVE; attach the MCP server.
MCP tools/list, then tools/call through the gateway.
Attach a Cedar policy that permits read-only tools and denies the write tool.
checks: write tool is denied by policy
simplified: Cedar evaluation is simplified; check which policy features are enforced.
layers.outcome: One governed gateway with a tool catalogue and a read-only policy

layers.title: Actions and Approval
layers.objective: Make write actions safe: park the action for a human, record every decision, and only then execute.
learn: Risk levels: low auto-approves, medium and high need a human
Durable approval state and a callback
An approval ledger as the system of record; idempotency
build: Agent writes a PENDING row to the Firestore ledger and publishes the request to the work-order-approval topic.
The approver reads the approver-inbox subscription.
The approval-decision function checks the approver and records APPROVED or REJECTED.
The waiting caller polls the ledger; create-work-order runs only on APPROVED.
Prove: nothing is written before approval, and an unauthorised approver is rejected.
simplified: This is assembled from Pub/Sub, functions and Firestore: Google Cloud has no waitForTaskToken-style workflow primitive in this reference. Workflows is the managed alternative and is not used here.
layers.native: Assembled pattern, not a single managed service.
layers.outcome: Writes that wait for a human, with a ledger of every decision

layers.title: Access and Perimeter
layers.objective: Sign users in, carry their identity to every layer, and put a protected edge in front of the tools.
learn: Identity provider, sign-in and tokens
Verify the token at the edge
A web firewall and rate limits
build: Identity Platform: sign up and sign in to get an ID token; verify signature, audience and issuer.
Create a service account for the agent and generateIdToken.
Cloud Armor: create a security policy with a WAF rule.
API Gateway: create the API, config (OpenAPI with x-google-backend and JWT security) and gateway.
Invoke /search with a valid ID token.
checks: sign-in returns an ID token that verifies
simplified: Tokens are real signed JWTs; federation and MFA are simplified.
layers.outcome: Sign-in, a verified token and a protected API edge

layers.title: Channels and Input Guardrails
layers.objective: Let people reach the agent, filter what comes in, and tell approvers what is waiting.
learn: Input guardrails: prompt attacks and blocked terms
The approver inbox: a topic with a queue behind it
build: Create the Model Armor template facilities-guardrail (prompt injection, responsible-AI, sensitive data).
sanitizeUserPrompt: a normal question is allowed.
A prompt injection is blocked.
Create the approver-inbox subscription on the work-order-approval topic; publish, pull and acknowledge.
simplified: Model Armor is a deterministic filter set, not Google's trained classifiers.
layers.outcome: Input guardrails and an approver inbox

layers.title: AgentOps and Observability
layers.objective: See what the agent did: a trace per step, metrics for KPIs, and structured logs tied to the trace.
learn: Spans per agent and per tool
Metrics and logs correlated by trace id
build: Cloud Trace v2 batch_write_spans: one span per agent or tool step.
Cloud Trace v1 get_trace and list_traces read it back.
Cloud Logging log_struct and list_entries, correlated with the trace.
Cloud Monitoring: create, write and list a custom metric.
simplified: Storage and query are simplified; alerting policies and SLOs are not simulated.
layers.outcome: Traces, metrics and logs you can read back

layers.title: Governance and Security
layers.objective: Protect and audit the whole app: encrypt the sensitive records and prove who did what.
learn: Envelope protection with an encryption context
An audit trail of the run and the approval events
build: Create the key ring facilities and key ledger-key with rotation.
Envelope-encrypt the approval record with additional authenticated data.
Prove decrypting with the wrong AAD is refused.
Cloud Audit Logs: admin activity for the run (CreateKeyRing, CreateCryptoKey) and the approval topic creation.
simplified: IAM evaluation is simplified; check the capability notes for what is enforced.
layers.outcome: Encrypted records and an audit trail of the run
